title: I Used the Aquarium Feeding Log on the Intern Who Pocketed My Squid

parts.text: I signed squid for tank 4 at 10:07 a.m. and intern Sage palmed the bag into a tote labeled TRAINING. The log said: SIGN THE PREY. FEED THE TANK. NO TRAINING HOLDS. I was twenty-one, feed volunteer, holding an empty bucket. Sage winked. "Interns are the diet." I photographed the empty line, the tote, and the hungry tank camera. Then I logged a hold. At 10:15 husbandry asked why Sage's tote was on tank 4's prey. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Husbandry can see Sage's training tote on tank 4's signed squid line.

social.video_title: The intern pocketed the squid into a training tote — Part 1/2
social.description: Aquarium, a feeding log, and an empty bucket. I logged the hold. Would you have photographed the tote?

parts.text: Sage called it enrichment until husbandry asked for the log. I printed the hold, the photo, and the prey line. Squid went in the tank. Sage enriched with labeled training stock and told interns enrichment was always about optics. Optics is a word totes use when a camera exists. Feeding now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE DIET. I keep tank 4. Sage labels. The water finally looks like a log, not a pocket. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
